Rakow Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Raków, Poland

Demolished. Raków, founded in 1567, was an important Arian and Calvinist center until the early 17th century; its owners, the Sienieńscy family, were favorable to Jewish settlement, and the community had its own synagogue as early as 1606. The Jewish population reached over 78 percent of the town by 1827. In 1942, young Jews were sent to work at the Hugo Schneider Aktiengesellschaft metalware factory in Skarżysko-Kamienna, while the rest of the community was deported to Treblinka. This cemetery, established at the beginning of the 17th century and enlarged in 1930 due to overcrowding, was almost completely destroyed by the Germans during WWII, its matzevot used for construction; the last burial likely took place in 1942, and the site was officially closed in 1957. In 2017, several dozen matzevot fragments recovered during the demolition of a barn and an abandoned building in the city were returned to the cemetery.
